grammar.title: 7B: Second conditional — choosing between conditionals
grammar.explanation:
The **second conditional** talks about imaginary situations. The shape is **if + past simple** in the condition, and **would/wouldn't + infinitive** in the result.

It describes the present or the future, never the past. *If I had more empathy, I would reconcile with my estranged brother* is a dream about now, not a memory.

In formal English, use **were** (not **was**) with I, he, she, and it. *If the proud patriarch were here, he would end the old feud* sounds more correct and more elegant.

**If I were you** is the classic way to give advice. *If I were you, I wouldn't alienate the people who love you* is softer than a direct order.

You can replace **would** with **could** when you mean possibility, not certainty. *If she tried, she could nurture the relationship back to life* suggests it is possible, not guaranteed.

Choosing between them is about reality. The **first conditional** is real and probable: *If I have time, I'll call my mother.* The **second conditional** is hypothetical: *If I had time, I'd call my mother.* One believes; the other dreams.

At C1 level, watch for **mixed conditionals**: a past condition with a present result. *If they hadn't become estranged, they would be close now* mixes **if + past perfect** with **would + infinitive**.

You can even drop **if** entirely. **Would + infinitive** alone can paint an imaginary scene: *A quiet family dinner without the old fallout would be wonderful.*
examples: *If I were* the patriarch of this family, *I would end* the feud today. (imaginary present)
*If she had shown* more empathy, *they would have reconciled* years ago. (past regret)
*If we nurtured* our kinship instead of our pride, *we wouldn't feel* so alienated. (imaginary present)
*If I were you*, *I'd call* your estranged brother this week. (advice)
*If their upbringing had been* gentler, *the fallout wouldn't be* so bitter now. (mixed: past condition, present result)
A peaceful reconciliation *would heal* more than any argument ever could. (imaginary wish, no if)

practice.q: Which conditional is this: 'If I had more time, I would visit my family'?
practice.a: Second conditional — a hypothetical present: if + past simple, would + infinitive.

practice.q: Make this real situation hypothetical: 'I don't have empathy for him, so we argue.'
practice.a: 'If I had more empathy for him, we wouldn't argue.'

practice.q: What is mixed about 'If they hadn't fought, they would be close now'?
practice.a: Mixed conditional — a past condition (if + past perfect) with a present result (would + infinitive).
